title: Polynomial resolutions under a derived tensor square
statement: Let $A\to C$, $A\to A'$, $f:C\to C'$ and $A'\to C'$ form a commutative square of commutative rings. Use ordinary-module derived categories $D(T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the derived scalar extension and its normalized extension/restriction adjunction obtained through the one-point-site identification [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification, lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let $\epsilon:P_\bullet\to C$ be any polynomial resolution in [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]: each $P_n$ is a polynomial $A$-algebra surjecting onto $C$, and its nonpositive alternating-face complex $S=s(P_\bullet)$ augments quasi-isomorphically to $C[0]$. Then $S$ has flat $A$-module terms and is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Under its canonical computation isomorphism $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\simeq Q(S\otimes_A A')$, the derived multiplication $\mu:C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to C'[0]$ (the adjunct of $f:C[0]\to\operatorname{Res}C'[0]$) is represented by the chain augmentation $\epsilon'$, zero in negative degrees and given by $p\otimes a'\mapsto f(\epsilon(p))a'$ in degree zero. If $\mu$ is a quasi-isomorphism, the canonical ring map $\alpha:C\otimes_A A'\to C'$, $c\otimes a'\mapsto f(c)a'$, is an isomorphism, the canonical map $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to(C\otimes_A A')[0]$ is $\alpha^{-1}\mu$, and $P'_\bullet=P_\bullet\otimes_A A'\to C'$ with augmentation $\epsilon'$ is a polynomial resolution over $A'$. Tensor and scalar extension mean [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-module-base-change]. No flatness of the ring maps is assumed. Flat modules are as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and simplicial objects and their morphisms are as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object].

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), proof using the free resolution s(P) and its tensor augmentation; the degree-zero pushout identification makes explicit the reduction for a general commutative square.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-simplicial-tensor-model] with $B=C$ and the given augmentation. Its hypotheses require only termwise polynomiality and surjectivity, both included in the resolution hypothesis. It gives flat terms of $S$, polynomial terms of $P'_\bullet=P_\bullet\otimes_A A'$, a termwise surjective augmentation $q':s(P'_\bullet)\to(C\otimes_A A')[0]$, and the identity comparison $S\otimes_A A'=s(P'_\bullet)$ carrying $\epsilon\otimes1$ to $q'$. Write $U=C\otimes_A A'$ and $T=S\otimes_A A'$.

The given $\epsilon:S\to C[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $S^i=0$ for $i>0$. Apply [lem-trf-flat-resolution-canonical-tensor-comparison] with $N=C$, bound $b=0$, and the flat terms from Step 1. It makes $S$ K-flat and supplies $j:QT\xrightarrow{\sim}C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ with $\gamma_{C[0]}j=Q(\epsilon\otimes1)=Qq'$, where $\gamma$ is the canonical derived-to-ordinary map. Thus the computation isomorphism in the statement is $j^{-1}$, with its prescribed counit normalization.

Set $g=f\epsilon:S\to\operatorname{Res}C'[0]$. Apply the representative formula (2) in [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], transported to ordinary modules by [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification]. Its hypotheses hold because Step 2 gives K-flatness and Step 1 gives flat terms. Naturality of adjunction with respect to $Q\epsilon$ identifies the adjunct of $Qf$ after precomposition with $L(Q\epsilon)$ with the adjunct of $Qg$. Under the computation at $S$ the latter is the chain map $h:T\to C'[0]$, zero in negative degrees, with $h^0(p\otimes a')=f(\epsilon_0(p))a'$. Hence $\mu j=Qh$. The tensor relations and commutativity of the ring square define a unital ring map $\alpha:U\to C'$ by $c\otimes a'\mapsto f(c)a'$. On pure tensors $h=\alpha[0]q'$, so $\mu=\alpha[0]\gamma_{C[0]}$ by Step 2 and cancellation of $j$.

Compute degree zero using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Since $S$ has zero positive terms, $C=\operatorname{coker}(d:S^{-1}\to S^0)$ via $\epsilon_0$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identifies $H^0(T)=T^0/\operatorname{im}(d\otimes1)$ with $U$: a balanced bilinear map $S^0\times A'\to M$ vanishes on $(dx,a')$ exactly when it descends to $C\times A'$. Thus the quotient and $C\otimes_A A'$ have the same universal property, and the resulting isomorphism is $[p\otimes a']\mapsto\epsilon_0(p)\otimes a'$. Under it $H^0(h)=\alpha$. If $\mu$ is invertible, $Qh=\mu j$ is invertible. Applying $H^0$ therefore makes the underlying $A'$-linear map of $\alpha$ bijective. A bijective unital ring homomorphism has a ring-homomorphic inverse: apply its injectivity to the addition, multiplication and unit identities. Hence $\alpha$ is a ring isomorphism.

Step 3 gives $\gamma_{C[0]}=\alpha[0]^{-1}\mu$, proving the asserted equality with the canonical map. The augmentation of $P'_\bullet$ to $C'$ is $\alpha\epsilon'_U$, where $\epsilon'_U$ is the augmentation to $U$ from Step 1; its alternating chain map is exactly $h$. Polynomiality and surjectivity of every augmentation to $U$ were supplied by [lem-trf-polynomial-simplicial-tensor-model]; composition with the isomorphism $\alpha$ preserves surjectivity. Finally $Qh=\mu j$ is invertible, so every $H^r(h)$ is an isomorphism by the cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The polynomial-resolution criterion of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] now applies: $P'_\bullet\to C'$ is termwise polynomial and surjective and its alternating augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. No tensor functor was assumed exact.

Step 1: the tensor model applies with B=C and needs only polynomial terms and surjective epsilon_n. Step 2: the comparison applies with N=C, b=0, q=epsilon; the direction of j checks out. Step 3: f epsilon is A-linear because the square commutes. By adjunction naturality, formula (2) and c_S = gamma_S, mu j = Qh and mu = alpha[0] gamma. Step 4: right exactness is proved through the tensor universal property, using ker epsilon_0 = im d from the quasi-isomorphism with S^1=0; H^0(h)=alpha, so alpha is a ring isomorphism. Step 5: the canonical-map clause and the polynomial-resolution criterion are met by alpha epsilon'_U. Small cases tested: Z to F_p with C=A'=C'=F_p (the hypothesis fails, Tor_1 is nonzero, nothing false is concluded); C=A; A'=0; empty variable sets; flat base change. There are no new nodes.
